areas.label: Initialization lifetimes and register allocation
areas.evidence: Current baseline: 1236 bytes versus original 1232, approximate nmscore 69, local frame 172 bytes matching the original. Old shard65 notes (254/1220) predate this checkpoint. Compiler RTL with unchanged normal flags reproduces the complete 3540-byte standalone control object exactly (SHA256 50da7b6417a16d8e2cd7a53ca5986cc86f14b48e5dc22a3b9243596e3c0b8e75). GCSE replaces the initial h0 zero with the HI subreg of the twice-assigned text pseudo; reload adds an early word-zero store at SP+0x98 and a halfword reload. The original uses a fresh zero in r3 for h0 and stores frame at SP+0x94. Removing the early text zero loses its later spill home and reduces the frame to 168 bytes. Moving text=0 after h2=0 but before h0=0 gives exact 1232-byte size and the correct frame, yet rotates scratch registers through sprite initialization and differs in pool padding (score 78); it was rejected. Frame/text declaration order, signed/narrow/volatile types, chained zero assignments, different zero owners, a metadata aggregate and using text in the measure call did not improve the complete baseline. A strict-control 300-second two-job permuter search produced no improved candidate. Preserve the existing source; inspect the actual reload/REG_EQUIV behavior before retrying these hypotheses.
